tldr: Eight US states sued OpenAI over ChatGPT's safety for children, while an OpenAI engineer was arrested for allegedly planting a $14 recording device in an executive conference room and a judge signalled an injunction for Apple in its trade-secret fight.

ASML beat on Q3 profit (net income about EUR 4.96B) and lifted its 2026 sales floor to EUR 44B, yet chip stocks fell for a sixth session (SOX -3.1%) as SK hynix dropped 5% on CXMT's server-memory push, CoreWeave sank about 15% with bond yields near 15%, and Dell fell about 11% on a Barclays downgrade.

In China, 151 apps (65 Tencent, 23 Alibaba) refused ByteDance's Doubao phone agent, StepFun priced its STEPX Neo agent phone at 3,999 yuan, and DeepSeek's funding round was reported to double to about 100B yuan.

items.title: Eight US states sue OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT harms children and was marketed as safe
items.summary: Attorneys general from eight states sued OpenAI on Oct 14 over ChatGPT's safety for minors. Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska and West Virginia announced suits at a joint press conference, while Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho and Montana filed separately in their own state courts. Iowa's suit invokes its Consumer Fraud Act and alleges OpenAI falsely portrayed ChatGPT as safe for ages 13 and up. The states seek court orders changing how ChatGPT treats young users, plus civil penalties and damages.
items.why_it_matters: It is the first multi-state litigation wave against a frontier lab on child safety, following Florida's lone suit in June. It raises OpenAI's legal and product-compliance exposure on age gating and youth features.

items.title: FBI arrests OpenAI engineer charged with planting hidden recording device in executive conference room
items.summary: The Justice Department charged Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan after OpenAI staff found a roughly $14 ESP32-based device hidden in toilet paper behind a TV in a San Francisco executive conference room, installed around Sept 28. Prosecutors say a ChatGPT account tied to his spouse was used for prompts on building and hiding such a device, and Bloomberg reports a court filing shows a one-way ticket to Saudi Arabia booked for Oct 12. OpenAI fired him and said it saw no sign of access to model weights, source code or customer data.
items.why_it_matters: A physical-security and insider-threat incident at the most prominent US lab, amid scrutiny of AI-lab security. The complaint does not allege trade-secret theft or acting for a foreign government.

items.title: Doubao phone assistant opens screen automation after 30-day notice; 151 apps, incl. 65 Tencent and 23 Alibaba, opt out
items.summary: ByteDance's Doubao phone assistant said the 30-day public-notice period for its Screen Automation Execution Protocol ended on Oct 14 and it will gradually open screen-automation permissions for third-party apps. Apps that declared a refusal will not be operated by the agent, and the platform acts within 3 working days of a refusal. The latest list shows 151 refusing apps, including WeChat, Taobao, Alipay, Meituan, Kuaishou, DeepSeek and Kimi. Media say the block only stops the AI's GUI recognition and simulated taps; the apps still work manually.
items.why_it_matters: The largest Chinese super-apps are refusing to let a rival's phone agent drive their interfaces, showing how hard open agent-to-app access is without formal APIs.

items.title: ASML Q3 profit beats, raises 2026 sales floor to EUR 44B; customers float orders for 2029-2030
items.summary: ASML reported Q3 net sales of EUR 11.66B and net income of about EUR 4.96B (versus 4.1B expected), guided Q4 sales of EUR 14.2-15.2B and lifted the low end of its 2026 range to EUR 44-45B. CEO Christophe Fouquet said some customers are asking about orders for 2029 and 2030 and the company is looking at expanding capacity beyond its earlier 30% increase for 2028. SCMP reports China sales rose 109% quarter on quarter, to 23% of machine sales from 14%.
items.why_it_matters: The strongest read-through yet that AI capex still pulls through lithography demand despite a chip-stock rout, and a sign of Chinese stockpiling ahead of possible tighter DUV export rules.

items.title: Judge says Apple injunction 'highly likely' as OpenAI alleges ex-employee took 100+ device files to Apple
items.summary: At a hearing in Apple's trade-secret suit against OpenAI, the judge said he is highly likely to grant a preliminary injunction barring use of Apple proprietary information by former employees now at OpenAI, per Bloomberg. OpenAI countered in a filing that a former employee who returned to Apple sent more than 100 files about an unreleased device to personal accounts and presented OpenAI product plans to Apple leadership. Apple disputes the claim. A day earlier a judge ordered OpenAI to turn over hiring records in the case.
items.why_it_matters: The case bears on OpenAI's consumer-hardware push and on Silicon Valley hiring norms; an injunction would constrain engineers moving between the two companies.

items.title: SK hynix falls 5% as China's CXMT targets server memory; chip index slides for a sixth session
items.summary: SK hynix fell about 5%, Western Digital 4% and Micron 3% on Oct 14 after CXMT signalled a denser chip design aimed at server memory, which it aims to introduce by year-end; analysts say hyperscaler qualification is the hurdle. items.title: Apple to launch limited Apple Intelligence in mainland China in December, Bloomberg reports
items.summary: Bloomberg reports Apple will release Apple Intelligence in mainland China in December with iOS 27.3 after a long regulatory delay, without the new Siri AI assistant and other features announced this year. Initial features reportedly cover Genmoji, notification summaries, writing tools and Photos Clean Up. Alibaba's Qwen models are involved, and Apple must let Chinese authorities approve ongoing model updates. Apple has not confirmed.
items.why_it_matters: Opens Apple's biggest contested market to on-device AI and is a win for Alibaba's Qwen, but the stripped-down feature set leaves Apple behind local AI phones.

items.title: Anthropic details Scion, an in-house git replacement built after merges grew from 2,500 to 30,000+ a day
items.summary: Anthropic's engineering blog says merges to its monorepo rose from about 2,500 per day in May 2026 to over 30,000 by September, with nearly all clients being always-online agents and CI jobs. Seven engineers built a server-heavy version control system called Scion, plus a review tool called Antique, and migrated in five months. Anthropic says it cut CPU and memory use about 200x versus the old git mirrors, with cache hit rates above 99%, and that Scion is not planned as a public product.
items.why_it_matters: A frontier lab reports that agent-driven code volume has outgrown git's offline-client assumptions; source control and review are becoming the bottleneck for AI-assisted engineering.

items.title: OpenAI's Sachin Katti to leave infrastructure role; Uday Ruddarraju to lead compute
